denial.text: Silverline Medicare Advantage denied the claim for CPT 27447 (total knee arthroplasty) with date of service 2026-09-04. CARC 50: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer. Payer remark: Documentation does not establish failure of conservative treatment prior to arthroplasty.

criteria.text: Radiographic evidence of advanced osteoarthritis: Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3 or 4, joint space narrowing to bone-on-bone contact, or deformity.

Failure of at least 3 months of conservative treatment including anti-inflammatory or analgesic medication, physical therapy or a supervised home exercise program, activity modification, and at least one intra-articular corticosteroid injection.
Pain with weight-bearing that interferes with activities of daily living, with limited range of motion or instability on examination.
Body mass index under 40, nicotine-free, and medically optimized for surgery.

chart.text: Patient called about a tick bite on the shoulder after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.
Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 17 and 15. No ocular pathology noted.

Referral letter from the primary care office. Thank you for seeing this patient of mine for evaluation. Her history and medication list are attached. Please let me know what you recommend and whether anything is needed from our end.

72 year old woman in orthopedic clinic for the left knee, hurting for 3 years and much worse this year. Discussed the options from more conservative care to replacement. Her history otherwise: anxiety, sees a counselor, mild asthma, albuterol maybe twice a year, hypertension on lisinopril. Allergies: sulfa, hives as a child. Does not smoke, a glass of wine on weekends, works as a teacher. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. Meloxicam 15 daily for the better part of a year, acetaminophen on top, gave up the yard work, uses a cane outdoors. Sending her to PT. Pain with every step, night pain that wakes her, cannot do stairs without the rail, cannot kneel or get out of a low chair without pushing up. Range of motion 5 to 105 degrees with crepitus, medial joint line tenderness, varus thrust with gait.

Standing AP, lateral, and sunrise views of the left knee. Complete loss of the medial joint space with bone-on-bone contact, large marginal osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis and cysts, 7 degrees of varus. Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.
PT evaluation, left knee osteoarthritis. Quad strengthening, range of motion, gait training with the cane. Plan 8 weeks.
Session 2. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, she reports no real change.
Work note requested for a sick day last Thursday. Faxed to the employer.
Session 3. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, she reports about the same.

Twisted the right ankle stepping off a curb 5 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.
Session 4. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, she reports slight improvement that does not last.
Intra-articular corticosteroid injection, left knee, triamcinolone 40 with lidocaine, anterolateral approach. Tolerated well.
Session 5. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, she reports about the same.
Session 6. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, she reports no real change.
Blood pressure check. 125 over 87 today, 145 over 75 on repeat. She has been taking the lisinopril 20 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 6 weeks.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.

Called her with the cholesterol results. Total 206, LDL 144, HDL 61, triglycerides 135. Discussed diet and walking. She wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.
Interval visit. Nothing new since last time, symptoms as described before, she is managing. Went over the plan again and answered questions from her spouse.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 7 years.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.

Back to decide on the left knee. Recommended total knee arthroplasty. Reviewed the operation, the hospital stay, the rehab, and the risks including infection and clot. Vitals today 136 over 81, pulse 74. Finished 8 weeks of PT, the injection gave about 3 weeks of relief, still on the meloxicam, still using the cane. That is 4 months of conservative care without durable benefit. BMI 35, never smoked, A1c 6.3, dental clearance in the chart.
Nurse call. Patient had questions about time off work and whether she needs someone at home the first night. Answered both, she will arrange it.

Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, she will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.
Pre-op. Medical clearance in the chart. Hold the meloxicam a week out. Consent signed for left total knee arthroplasty.

Mole on the left forearm that her spouse noticed. About 7 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change she is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.
Vitamin D came back 20. Started 2000 units daily, recheck in three months. Also talked about calcium from food rather than pills.

expected.note: The chart documents every criterion; the CARC 50 denial can be answered from the record.
